findings.reason: the case must assert what the fix actually changes (the queued pointer's `manifest_path` and `node.manifest_path` still name the request's original run directory), or it is a green line that cannot go red.
findings.text: §17's done-when requires that "No second run directory exists under the runs home afterwards", but no dispatch path creates a run directory on a re-dispatch: the only `run_dir(...).mkdir` on that path is at `dispatch.py:2782`, reached only after the queued branch has already returned at `dispatch.py:2300`, so the assertion holds on the unfixed code and measures nothing

findings.reason: a node told to place the constant beside `queue_dispatch` has no grant to edit `runs.py`, so it either stops for a scope change or puts the constant somewhere the plan did not ask for.
findings.text: the write paths read "`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` (for `queue_dispatch`, if it lives there)", but `queue_dispatch` is defined at `reckon/crew/runs.py:686` and `runs.py` is not a write path, while the deliverable at line 193 instructs the node to "Name the steerable fields once, beside `queue_dispatch`"

findings.reason: a merge at the record's top level cannot both carry the new done-when and keep the old manifest path, so the plan must say the split applies within `node` and name the field of the node it preserves; otherwise the very field the incident repointed is left out of the merge.
findings.text: §17 splits the record into steerable fields (goal, done-when, negative control, write paths, inputs, time budget, dispatch options) and identity fields (run id, run directory, `manifest_path`, session, `base_sha`, created time), but the steered fields and `manifest_path` all live inside the nested `node` mapping: `_queued_request_record` (`dispatch.py:205-255`) writes `"node": node.as_dict()` with no top-level `manifest_path`, and the launch reads the path from `record["node"]["manifest_path"]` (`dispatch_sessions.py:1006`)

findings.reason: the missing capability sits in `claims.py`, which the section already declares as a write path, and done-when case 1 ("with source `repair-round`") fails until the source is recorded, so the node corrects itself without a scope or design change.
findings.text: §18 says the round uses `claims.widen_claim` "with source `repair-round` … so `dispatch_claims.declared_write_grants` lists it", but `widen_claim` records a grant only through `_record_self_grant` (`claims.py:146-155`), which runs only when `self_widen=True` and hardcodes `"source": "worker"`; called the way `crew widen` calls it (`crew_run_commands.py:1491`, `self_widen` unset) the path lands in `node["write_paths"]` — enough for promotion to accept it — but no grant entry is written, so `declared_write_grants` reports the path with source `dispatch`

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §17's write path `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py (for queue_dispatch, if it lives there)` names the wrong module: `queue_dispatch` is defined at `reckon/crew/runs.py:686`, and `runs.py` appears in no write path.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §17's second done-when case ("No second run directory exists under the runs home afterwards") passes on the unfixed code, because the re-dispatch path never creates a run directory.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections write their gates to `tests/` in the repository, and every evidence anchor the changed `_document` comments cite resolves inside `docs/evidence/archive/work-is-never-stuck-behind-the-admission-loop-landed.html`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §17 and §18 name no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag in the files or symbols they add, and `repair-round` is a data value recorded in a grant, not a label carried into a symbol.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §17's identity/steerable split is stated against top-level record fields, but the manifest path it must preserve and the goal/done-when/write-paths it must replace all live inside `record["node"]`; and §18 says the round calls `claims.widen_claim` "with source `repair-round`", a source that mechanism has no parameter for.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §17 carries one deliverable (merge only the steerable fields of a queued request) and §18 one (record the repair round's extra paths on the run's claim before resuming).
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §17 and §18 declare no `plan-section-depends-on` entry and need none: each edits a mechanism no other section owns (`_answer_existing_node_run` in dispatch.py, `_repair_resume_advice` in recovery_repair_dispatch.py), and both appear as `implementable` in `plan-section-declarations` consistently with their own `data-status`.
